Getting Artificial Turf Around a Pool Right in Kissimmee

Artificial turf around a pool in Kissimmee replaces the strip of St. Augustine that quits once a screen enclosure blocks the sun. Installed turf runs $8 to $18 a square foot as of September 2026, glued to the pool deck or lanai floor over a drainage underlay, or seamed over a graded base beside it, usually in two to four days.

Reviewed by Luis Austin, owner · Last reviewed September 21, 2026

Who this fits, and who should look elsewhere

Artificial turf around a pool solves one specific problem: the strip of ground between the deck and the fence that never gets full sun once a screen enclosure goes up, or the slab inside the cage where nothing was ever meant to grow. It suits pool homes in Kissimmee, St. Cloud and Hunters Creek where St. Augustine has thinned out behind the cage, lanais where the floor is bare concrete, and rental homes that need the yard to look finished in every listing photo without a mowing crew scheduled around guests.

It doesn't fit every pool yard. If the area between the deck and a retention pond is already a planted buffer, turf isn't the answer there, because the state's synthetic turf standard keeps it 10 feet back from a lake, pond or canal unless a seawall or bulkhead already lines the bank (a swimming pool itself doesn't trigger that setback; an open pond behind the pool cage does). And if you're picturing turf that feels cool underfoot at two in the afternoon in July, that's not how any dark synthetic surface in full sun behaves, ours included. More on that below, honestly, not glossed over.

Pool turf options: deck border, lanai floor, and paver joints

"Pool turf" covers a few different builds depending on what's under it. A border between the deck and the fence line gets a base of washed, open-graded crushed rock, compacted firm without packing the native sand underneath so tight that it quits draining, the same as any side yard build. A screen enclosure or lanai floor is almost always bare concrete, so the turf gets glued down instead of seamed over soil. A narrow accent strip between pavers at the pool is a different job again: a ribbon of turf cut to width and set into the joint rather than a walking surface.

AreaTypical buildSuited to

Chlorine and saltwater in normal splash amounts don't discolor or break down the fibers; concentrated pool chemicals spilled straight onto turf can, so store shock and acid away from the edge and hose off any spill.

Can turf go inside a screen enclosure or next to a saltwater pool?

Yes to both. Inside a screen enclosure, turf is glued directly to the existing concrete slab over a thin drainage underlay, since there's no soil there to build a normal base from. Saltwater and chlorine splash don't damage the polyethylene fibers used in landscape turf; fiber makers test against pool chemistry and salt exposure and report no fading or breakdown from ordinary contact (chlorine-resistance testing summary). Standing puddles of pool water on the turf just need a rinse, same as a wet deck.

The detail that trips up a DIY glue-down is drainage. A pool cage floor has nowhere for water to go except an existing deck drain, so the underlay has to route splash and rinse water to that drain rather than letting it pool underneath the turf and turn sour. Seams inside a cage run parallel to the screen frame, not across the path people walk, so foot traffic doesn't work them open over time.

How we build turf on a pool deck or lanai floor

  1. Check the existing slope. Pool decks and lanai floors are already pitched to a drain. We confirm it still runs the right direction before anything new goes down.
  2. Clean and prep the slab. The concrete gets pressure washed, and any curling paint, sealer or old adhesive residue comes off so the new glue bonds to bare concrete.
  3. Lay the drainage underlay. A thin perforated mat goes down first so splash, rinse and any wind-blown rain reach the deck drain instead of collecting under the turf.
  4. Glue rather than nail. Turf on concrete is bonded with polyurethane adhesive along every edge and seam; there's no way to drive a perimeter nail into a slab.
  5. Seam away from the walking path. Seams are placed parallel to the cage frame so the heaviest foot traffic, not the glue line, takes the wear.
  6. Cut around posts and drains. Screen posts, drain covers and skimmer lids get trimmed around and left fully accessible for service.
  7. Light infill, brush, first rinse. A light infill and an initial hose-down settle the blades before we walk every seam one more time.

What artificial turf around a pool costs in Kissimmee

Pool-area turf prices from the same $8–$18 per square foot range as any residential job, with most yards landing between $10–$16. Glue-down work over an existing slab usually prices toward the top of that range rather than the middle, because there's no excavation to offset the adhesive labor and drainage underlay. Say a 500 sq ft lanai gets glued to the existing floor: at $16 to $18 a square foot for that kind of work, the job runs roughly $8,000 to $9,000, higher than the same square footage would cost as an open backyard border.

Open deck borders and turf between pavers price closer to the middle of the range, since they're built the normal way, over a compacted washed-rock base rather than glued to concrete. The full cost guide breaks the range down further by yard size, and this piece on installing over concrete, pavers or grass goes into the labor difference in more depth.

Heat, storms and window glare next to the pool

Be honest about heat before you commit a whole pool deck border to turf. In full Florida summer sun, synthetic turf commonly reaches 120 to 150°F at the surface and can go higher; a 30-second hose rinse drops that 30 to 50 degrees within minutes (Florida installer measurements). A pool deck already gets hot underfoot in July, concrete included, but bare feet moving from tile to turf will notice the difference at midday. Shade sails, a lighter infill color and a rinse before pool time help; an unshaded, west-facing strip is a place we'll say so upfront.

Perforated turf backing drains faster than 30 inches of water an hour (manufacturer FAQ on drainage rate), well beyond what a Central Florida summer storm delivers, but a glue-down lanai floor is only as good as the deck drain it feeds. If that drain is already slow, turf won't fix it. Window and door glass near a pool cage, especially large west- or south-facing sliders in newer pool homes, can reflect enough concentrated sunlight to soften synthetic turf; turf can melt from that kind of reflected glare, so we check nearby glass before quoting. Sprinkler heads that used to water the strip behind the cage get capped once turf goes down; the state's 2026 turf rule doesn't allow an in-ground system to irrigate synthetic turf.

HOA rules and Florida law for turf around a pool

Florida’s HB 683 and the adopted DEP rule that carries it out, Rule 62-308.100, apply to turf on a single-family lot of an acre or less, and a pool deck or lanai on that kind of lot is covered. The standard requires permeable turf free of intentionally added PFAS and heavy metals, keeps turf out of a tree's drip line without an arborist's sign-off, and keeps it at least 10 feet from the ordinary water line of a lake, pond or canal unless the bank already has a seawall or bulkhead. A swimming pool itself isn't a waterbody under that rule; a retention pond behind the pool cage is. Most pool cages sit well inside a fenced backyard, which is also the part of the lot Florida law protects from HOA restriction when it isn't visible from the street or a neighboring parcel.

None of that is legal advice, and the rule itself creates no new DEP permit; what still varies by city and county is the permit for the underlying screen enclosure or deck work. The permit guide lists what each Osceola, Orange, Polk, Lake and Seminole office asks for.

What goes wrong with a bad pool-turf install

  • Nailed edges on concrete. A perimeter can't be nailed into a slab; if it was, expect the edge to lift within a season.
  • No drainage underlay. Water sits under the turf inside the cage, and the space starts to smell like standing pool runoff.
  • Seams cut across the traffic path. The heaviest foot traffic on a lanai runs straight through the middle, and a seam placed there opens faster than one placed to the side.
  • Screen posts and drain lids ignored. Turf trimmed loosely around a post or drain leaves a gap that collects debris and gives ants a way in.
  • Wrong infill choice. A basic silica infill holds chlorine residue and salt spray longer than a coated or antimicrobial infill does in a splash zone, and the state standard limits a house lot to natural infill anyway: clean silica, zeolite or a non-toxic coated sand, not a rubber or synthetic product.

Caring for turf around a pool

Rinse chemical splash and leaf litter off with a hose rather than letting it dry into the fibers, and keep shock, acid and other concentrated pool chemicals stored away from the turf's edge. Brush the path from the lounge chairs to the pool steps a few times a year so the blades don't mat flat where everyone walks. After a named storm, walk the glued edges and any seam near the screen frame; the state standard requires edges and seams to be anchored against wind and flooding, and a lifted corner caught early is a small repair rather than a redo. A yearly power-broom and infill top-up keeps a pool-deck lawn looking the way it did on day one.

How do you find the best pool turf installer near you in Kissimmee?

Ask specifically about the parts of a pool job that a regular lawn install doesn't cover. Does the quote say the lanai floor gets glued, or does it just say "installed"? Is there a named drainage underlay, or is that assumed? How does the crew plan to route water to the existing deck drain, and what happens to the screen posts and skimmer lids during the cut? A written answer to those four questions tells you more than any claim about who's the top choice in town, and it lets you compare two bids on the same terms.

Questions people ask

Will pool chemicals ruin artificial turf if I spill some?

Diluted splash and everyday chlorine or salt exposure don't damage landscape turf, but a concentrated spill of shock, acid or algaecide can discolor or stiffen the fibers where it lands. Keep chemical containers off the turf and rinse any spill right away.

Can turf run right up to the pool coping?

Yes, if there's a firm edge to glue or nail into. Against loose gravel or a soft coping edge, we add a paver or metal edge strip first so the turf has something solid to anchor to.

Does turf make a wet pool deck more slippery?

Not more than wet tile or wet concrete. The backing is permeable, so water passes through rather than sitting on the surface, but any wet surface near a pool still calls for the usual care around the steps.

Can turf go over pavers inside a lanai instead of bare concrete?

Yes. Well-set pavers take turf almost the same way a slab does, usually with a thin leveling layer first. Loose or shifting pavers need to be reset before turf goes down, or the turf will telegraph the movement.

Do you cap the sprinkler heads near the pool deck?

Yes, any head that used to water the strip behind the cage gets capped at the line once turf replaces that area. The 2026 state turf standard doesn't allow an in-ground system to irrigate synthetic turf.

How hot does pool-deck turf get compared to the pavers around it?

Both get hot in full sun; turf can reach 120 to 150°F, similar to dark pavers or stamped concrete in the same exposure. A rinse cools either surface quickly, which is why a hose bib near the pool matters more than the surface choice.

Is turf a problem for a pool near a retention pond?

Only near the pond, not near the pool. The state's setback keeps synthetic turf at least 10 feet from the water line of a pond, lake or canal unless a seawall or bulkhead is already built along it, so we hold the turf back from an open bank and treat the pool-side area normally.
